title: Fires With No One Trapped
titleLabel: Fireground command should put firefighter safety first

title: Taichung factory fire: no one trapped,
yet firefighters were sent in
taichung.body: At 1:48 a.m., a fire broke out at a sheet-metal factory in Daya, Taichung. Although the scene had been confirmed to have “no one trapped,” the commander still sent firefighters inside to find the source of the fire. Within 10 minutes, thick smoke had built up, and two firefighters were trapped and killed.

alt.clipping: United Daily News clipping, Oct. 4, 2019: “No one trapped, but the fire must still be controlled”

title: Pingtung: Ming Yang International
stored excess chemicals, sparking a fire
pingtung.body: At 5:31 p.m., a fire broke out at a Ming Yang International warehouse. The company had illegally stored the chemical foaming agent C40-P at 30 times the permitted safety limit, and the room temperature exceeded the safe storage temperature. Four firefighters who went in to rescue people believed to be trapped were thrown by the blast wave, burned and struck by flying debris, and died after being taken to hospital.

title: Taoyuan: Chin-Poon Industrial breached fire compartments,
letting the fire spread with ease
taoyuan.body: At 9:28 p.m., flames erupted at the Chin-Poon factory. The company had illegally run exhaust ducts through the walls, breaching the fire compartments without authorization, and firefighters only discovered unidentified solvents stored on site after they arrived. Working from information that did not match the actual conditions, the firefighters became trapped and could not get out in time. Six died.
